## SAN RAFAEL CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT

Department: City Clerk's Office

Prepared by: Lindsay Lara, City Clerk

City Manager Approval:  \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

## TOPIC:

BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COMMITTEES INTERVIEWS

SUBJECT:

INTERVIEW  APPLICANTS  AND  MAKE  APPOINTMENTS  TO  THE  BOARD  OF LIBRARY TRUSTEES AND THE FIRE COMMISSION TO THE END OF OCTOBER 2029

## RECOMMENDATION:

Interview applicants and make appointments to the Board of Library Trustees, Fire Commission, Police Advisory and Accountability Committee, and the Planning Commission.

## BACKGROUND:

The City of San Rafael actively recruits community members to serve on its boards, commissions, and committees  to  ensure  broad  representation  and  public  input  in  City  policy  and  decision-making. Vacancies  occur  periodically  due  to  term  expirations,  resignations,  or  newly  created  positions.  The following members' terms are set to expire at the end of October 2025:

Alex Vahdat, Board of Library Trustees (1 st of two terms) Jaimi Cortez, Board of Library Trustees (2 nd of two terms - terming out) Ken Johnson, Fire Commission (1 st  of two terms) Donna McCusker, Fire Commission (1 st  of two terms) Daniel Alm, Police Advisory &amp; Accountability Committee (1 st of two terms) Fatai Tokolahi, Police Advisory &amp; Accountability Committee (1 st of two terms) Marilyn Alvarez, Police Advisory &amp; Accountability Committee Youth Member (1 st  of two terms) Jill Rodby, Planning Commissioner, District 1 (1 st of three terms)

Additionally there is a vacant seat on the Planning Commission for District 4, of which we have received no applications to date.

The City Clerk's Office conducts outreach for each vacancy through the City's website, social media channels,  email  subscription  lists,  and  MarinIJ.  Interested  residents  submit  an  application,  which  is reviewed and scheduled for interviews by the City Council.

SAN RAFAEL

## ANALYSIS:

Staff recommends the City Council interview applicants, and make appointments to two terms on the Board of Library Trustees and two terms on the Fire Commission, and any alternate terms as needed.

| Board of Library Trustees   | Fire Commission     |
|-----------------------------|---------------------|
| Alexander Vahdat            | Donna McCusker      |
| Caroline Doyle              | Kenneth Johnson     |
| Michael Polk                | Robert Mittelstaedt |

## Board of Library Trustees:

The term of Alexander Vahdat and Jaimi Cortes is set to expire at the end of October 2025. Alexander Vahdat is eligible for another term, however, Jaimi Cortes was ineligible because she has completed two consecutive terms and is terming-off of the Board of Library Trustees. Seven applications were received for the Board of Library Trustees; however, two applicants withdrew, and two applicants never responded to Staff to schedule interviews and confirm interest in serving.

The term of Donna McCusker and Kenneth Johnson is set to expire at the end of October 2025. Both incumbents are eligible for another term and have both reapplied. Six applications were received for the Fire  Commission;  however,  one  applicant  withdrew,  and  two  applicants  never  responded  to  Staff  to schedule interviews and confirm interest in serving.

## COMMUNITY OUTREACH:

The recruitment process was publicly noticed on the City's website, through social media, in the City Manager's newsletter, and Marin IJ. Outreach was also extended to community partners and stakeholder groups to encourage broad participation.

## FISCAL IMPACT:

There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

## OPTIONS:

The City Council has the following options to consider on this matter:

1. Make appointments to each legislative body following the interview; including alternate members as needed.
2. Direct  the  City  Clerk's  office  to  continue  recruitment  for  certain  Boards,  Commissions  and Committees.

## Caroline Elizabeth Doyle

## Profile:

I am a graduate of the College of Marin where I studied theater and subsequently Early Childhood Education. I have always been bright, creative, nurturing, confident, well spoken and well read, gentle, inclusive, and very joyous. I have found these traits to align well with connecting with and educating children.

## Experience:

## Teacher

November 2015 to Present

For the past five years I have been a teacher in a twoÕs classroom at the Marin Commons campus of Bright Horizons. Throughout most of this time I have team taught under a lead teacher, but I have maintained my classroom independently. In my five years I have built an early learning environment that has successfully and beautifully fostered the development of each child and which celebrates them. I supported this in the writing and implementing of age appropriate weekly curricula and facilitating and documenting the learning, joy, and milestones of my students. I built mindful and loving relationships with children and their families and other teachers as well and I kept open communication both written and verbally.

## Resource Teacher

November 2015 to November 2016

Between two Bright Horizons campuses; Marin Commons and Marin Day School I provided flex assistance in each of their classrooms ranging from the infant program through kindergarten preparation. I had a unique opportunity gain familiarity, knowledge, and love of a wide variety of ages and people.

## Program Leader

September 2013 to Present

I provide before school care at a local San Anselmo based elementary school through the Marin YMCA. In this position I provide supervision and structure yet bring a bright and engaging element to each day. I work with children aged four to ten.

## Extracurricular Work and Accomplishments

Reading Buddy

September 2017 to Present

I volunteer at the San Rafael Public Library once per week where elementary school aged read children aloud to me. The program is designed mainly to support students who are learning English as a second language and provides them an opportunity outside of school to develop their reading abilities. In addition to gaining weekly practice at reading and speaking in English I strive to help these children build vocabularies and increase their retention and understanding.

College of Marin Drama Department Secretary, 2011 to 2013

College of Marin Drama Department Most Outstanding Contribution , 2011

## Q21

Why are you interested in serving on a board or commission?

I enjoy engaging in activities surrounding libraries, I visit  the SR library often to check out books, DVDs, do research. I also do extensive historical research at the Marin Library, many university and public libraries in the Bay Area and elsewhere in the country. I worked several library settings including establishing a library for the Anthropology Department at San Diego State and in a paid clerical position in the Science Library at Michigan State University. Also, having established and operated my own business in the cultural resources management business for 30 years, I served on many organizational boards during that time. I enjoyed and thrived those settings, serving as secretary and then president in a national trade association, and as a board member on another. In those positions I planned and carried out agendas and oversaw many different projects and activities.

## Q21

Why are you interested in serving on a board or commission?

Having served on the San Rafael Fire Commission for the past three years, I remain deeply committed to advancing fire safety and resilience in our community-especially given our location in a high-risk wildfire zone. With over 30 years of experience in risk management for large real estate portfolios across the United States and internationally, I bring a broad understanding of how communities can prepare for and respond to natural disasters, including wildfires.

My work as an insurance broker involves advising clients across diverse regions on risk mitigation strategies, emergency planning, and property protection. This global perspective allows me to contribute informed, forward-thinking insights to the Commission's work -grounded in both best practices and real-world application. I'm passionate about continuing to serve San Rafael by helping shape policies and initiatives that protect lives, property, and the long-term resilience of our city.

Fire Commission

## Q22

Describe possible areas in which you may have a conflict of interest with the City:

I do not have any known conflicts of interest with the City of San Rafael. I do not hold any financial interests, contractual relationships, or affiliations that would interfere with my ability to serve objectively and in the best interest of the community. My professional work in risk management and insurance is conducted with full transparency and does not involve any direct business with the City itself. I remain committed to upholding the integrity and impartiality required of this role.

## Minutes subject to approval at the 10/06/25 City Council Meeting

## MINUTES

## SAN RAFAEL CITY COUNCIL - MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 15, 2025

## REGULAR MEETING AT 6:00 P.M. San Rafael City Hall, Council Chambers 1400 Fifth Avenue, San Rafael, CA 94901

## Watch Online: Watch on Webinar: https://tinyurl.com/city-council-2 Watch on YouTube: www.youtube.com/cityofsanrafael Listen by phone: (669) 444-9171 ID: 860-6190-5675#

This meeting will be held in-person. This meeting is being streamed to YouTube at www.youtube.com/cityofsanrafael.

How to participate in the meeting:

- You are welcome to come to the meeting and provide public comment in person. Each speaker will have 2-minutes to provide public comment per agenda item.
- Submit  your  comments  by email to  city.clerk@cityofsanrafael.org  by  4:00  p.m.  the  day  of  the meeting.

If you experience technical difficulties during the meeting, please contact city.clerk@cityofsanrafael.org.

Present: Vice Mayor Bushey Councilmember Hill Councilmember Kertz Councilmember Llorens Gulati Mayor Kate Absent: None Also Present: City Manager Cristine Alilovich City Attorney Robert Epstein City Clerk Lindsay Lara

Mayor Kate called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. and invited City Clerk Lindsay Lara to call the roll. All members of the City Council were present.

Mayor Kate provided opening remarks, which included gratitude to City Staff, the recent acts of political violence across our nation and a land acknowledgment.

City Clerk Lindsay Lara informed the community that the in-person meeting would be recorded and streamed  live  to  YouTube  and  through  Zoom,  and  that  there  would  be  Spanish  language interpretation.  She  noted  the  two-minute  timer  for  public  comment  and  closed  captioning  on Zoom.

## OPEN SESSION - THIRD FLOOR CONFERENCE ROOM

1. None.

## CLOSED SESSION - THIRD FLOOR CONFERENCE ROOM

2. Closed Session: - None.

## CITY MANAGER AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS:

## (including AB 1234 Reports on Meetings and Conferences Attended at City Expense)

3. City Manager and Councilmember Reports:

City Manager Cristine Alilovich provided the following announcements and updates:

- National Preparedness Month Proclamation - Appreciation to our Office of Emergency Services, Fire and Police Departments
- Transit Month and alternative commute options
- Major Development Projects Map on City website - Interactive map of all development projects in neighborhoods across San Rafael
- Tomorrow, the County Board of Supervisors meeting to consider funding for a potential City park at 620 Canal Street
- Chamber  of  Commerce  to  host  a  Level  Up  Marin  Employment  Expo  on  Thursday, September 25 at B Street Community Center, 4-7 p.m.
- San  Rafael  Library  at  the  Carnegie  Building  ribbon-cutting  celebration  to  be  held Saturday, September 20, 12-5 p.m.
- Announced upcoming community events:
- o West End Block Party to be held Friday, September 19 and Friday, September 26, downtown from F to G, 6-9 p.m.
- o Porchfest to be held Sunday, September 21, in the Gerstle Park neighborhood, 12-5 p.m.
- o Movies in the Park (The Wild Robot) to be held Friday, September 26, at Gerstle Park, 6:45-8:45 p.m.
- o Hops and Vines Stroll (presented by the Business Improvement District) to be held Saturday, September 27, downtown from Fourth to Lincoln, 2-6 p.m.
- o Marin Sanitary Service Customer Appreciation Day to be held Sunday, September 28, at 535 Jacoby Street, 9a.m. to 2 p.m.

## City Councilmember Reports:

- Vice Mayor Bushey reported on a Marin Transit board meeting, a Central Marin Sanitation Agency board meeting, the Marin Presiding Judge Breiner's Memorial Bench in Loch Lomond and a ribbon-cutting for the new playground at Peacock Gap Park.
- Councilmember Llorens Gulati reported on Marin Transit, the 9/11 remembrance ceremony, the Canal Alliance Leadership Academy graduation and announced the Coastal Cleanup Day to be held this Saturday, September 20 at Pickleweed at 9 a.m.
- Councilmember Kertz reported on the City/County Schools Quarterly meeting, the Ember Stomp event, the Aegis ribbon-cutting, Contempo's Annual BBQ, the AgeFriendly San Rafael meeting and announced the Marin Senior Fair to be held Wednesday, September 17.
- Councilmember Hill reported on the Aegis ribbon-cutting and the Sun Valley Neighborhood Association meeting.
- Mayor Kate commented that her Report was covered by the councilmembers.

Mayor Kate invited public comment; however, there was none.

## SAN RAFAEL CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT

Department: Community and Economic Development

Prepared by: Kristina Estudillo Principal Planner

City Manager Approval:  \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

TOPIC:

AGREEMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE DOMINICAN RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AND ASSOCIATED SUPPLEMENTAL FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 BUDGET APPROPRIATION

SUBJECT:

RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY  MANAGER  TO (1) EXECUTE A PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  ENVIRONMENTAL  SCIENCE ASSOCIATES (ESA) IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $675,221 FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE DOMINICAN RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT  PROJECT  (PLAN  23-081)  LOCATED  AT  ASSESSOR'S  PARCEL NUMBER (APN) 015-163-03 AND (2) APPROPRIATE SUPPLEMENTAL FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2025-2026 BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS TOTALING $675,221

## RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution authorizing the City Manager to (1) enter into a  professional  services  agreement  with  Environmental  Science  Associates (ESA) for  environmental consulting services in an amount not to exceed $675,221 and (2) appropriate supplemental fiscal year (FY) 2025-2026 Budget Appropriations totaling $675,221.

## BACKGROUND:

In  December  2023,  the  Community  and  Economic  Development  (CED)  Department  received  an application  for  a  residential  development  project  on  a  20.79-acre  site  located  at  the  intersection  of Magnolia Avenue and Deer Park Avenue (Dominican Residential Development Project). The applicant for the project is Dominican Valley LLC, and Dominican University previously owned the site and was part  of  the  Dominican  College  Campus  Development  Plan.  The  application  was  determined  to  be complete for the purposes of application processing in October 2024, and staff subsequently initiated the environmental review process.

The proposed Dominican Residential Development Project involves subdividing the project site into 50 parcels and constructing 50 residential units, along with 14 Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs). The 50 residential units include the following types of housing:

- 27 single-family homes, ranging from 2,612 to 3,215 square feet (sf)

- 17 townhomes, ranging from 1,150 to 1,390 sf

## SAN RAFAEL CITY COUNCIL AGENDA REPORT / Page: 2

- o 14 attached JADUs
- 6 duplex units consisting of 1,705 sf each

As part of the application review process, the CED Department has analyzed the project for compliance with California's Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Based on the preliminary review of the project, the CED Department has determined that a full-scope Environmental Impact Report (EIR) covering all the topical issues associated with the project must be prepared to comply with CEQA.

As the City lacks the capacity and subject matter expertise to conduct the EIR, on May 2, 2025, CED staff published a Request for Proposals (RFP) to identify a firm to undertake the CEQA review for this project. In response, the CED Department received proposals from four interested firms. CED staff then held a series of interviews in July 2025 to ascertain which firm is the most qualified to conduct the CEQA review for a project of this nature. Subsequently, CED staff identified ESA as the most qualified firm for this project based on their CEQA expertise, track record, experience with complex housing development projects, and familiarity with state housing legislation.

## ANALYSIS:

Adopting the proposed resolution will authorize the City Manager to execute a professional services agreement with ESA to complete an EIR for the Dominican Residential Development Project. CED staff selected ESA after undergoing a formal competitive procurement process, and CED staff have identified ESA as the best qualified firm to complete the work required. ESA's completion of an EIR will ensure that the Dominican Residential Development Project complies with CEQA, which in turn provides the City with a process to evaluate any environmental impacts of the project and strategies to address these impacts.

## FISCAL IMPACT:

Approval of the staff recommendation would authorize a professional services agreement with ESA in an amount not to exceed $675,221. The project applicant is responsible for any costs incurred by the City in  processing  their  application,  including  the  cost  of  an  environmental  consultant  conducting  CEQA review for their development application. Thus, a supplemental FY 2025-26 budget appropriation is being requested within the City's Development Services Fund (207) in the amount of $675,221 to reflect funding provided by the project applicant, as well as to appropriate funding for the proposed contract.  To cover CED staff time overseeing the accounting of this project, the CED Department will require the project applicant to pay an additional ten percent administrative fee as prescribed in the Master Fee Schedule.

## OPTIONS:

The City Council has the following options to consider on this matter:

1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into the agreement.
2. Authorize the City Manager to enter into the agreement with modifications.
3. Direct staff to return with more information.
4. Take no action.

## RECOMMENDED ACTION:

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution authorizing the City Manager to (1) enter into a  professional  services  agreement  with  Environmental  Science  Associates  (ESA)  for  environmental consulting services in an amount not to exceed $675,221 and (2) appropriate supplemental fiscal year (FY) 2025-2026 Budget Appropriations totaling $675,221.

## ATTACHMENTS:

1. Resolution
2. Professional Services Agreement with ESA

## RESOLUTION NO.

RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO (1) EXECUTE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE ASSOCIATES (ESA) IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $675,221 FOR ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE DOMINICAN RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (PLAN 23-081) LOCATED AT ASSESSOR'S PARCEL NUMBER (APN) 015-163-03 AND (2) APPROPRIATE SUPPLEMENTAL FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2025-2026 BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS TOTALING $675,221

WHEREAS , the City of San Rafael's Community and Economic Development (CED) Department is processing a Tentative Subdivision Map and Major Environmental Design Review application for the proposed Dominican Residential Development Project (PLAN23-081), located at Marin County Assessor's Parcel Number (APN) 015-163-03; and

WHEREAS , the project requires environmental review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); and

WHEREAS ,  CED  staff  published  a  Request  for  Proposals  (RFP)  for  preparation  of  CEQA documentation for the proposed project on May 2, 2025, and subsequently received four proposals from interested firms; and

WHEREAS, CED staff reviewed the proposals and held a series of interviews in July 2025 to ascertain which was the most qualified firm to conduct the environmental review for a project of this nature; and

WHEREAS, CED staff identified Environmental Science Associates (ESA) as the most qualified firm because of their experience with complex housing development projects, understanding of recent changes to State law, and their proposed approach; and

WHEREAS, the project applicant is responsible for reimbursing the City for the costs incurred by the City in processing its development application, including preparation of CEQA documents; and

WHEREAS , the cost of preparing the CEQA document for the Dominican Residential Development Project will be paid through a reimbursement agreement between the CED department and the project applicant.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED , that the City Council of the City of San Rafael finds the foregoing recitals are true and correct, and authorizes the City Manager or their designee to execute a professional services agreement with Environmental Science Associates (ESA) for an amount not to exceed $675,221; and

FURTHER RESOLVED , that the City Council authorizes supplemental budget appropriations of $675,221 within the Development Services Fund (207) to support these agreements, via increased planning fee revenues received from the Dominican Residential Development Project applicant.

## SECTION 2 Qualifications

## CEQA Documentation

Environmental Science Associates' (ESA) team has broad experience and expertise in all aspects of the CEQA process. We have prepared more than 20.000 environmental documents at varying levels of analysis-exemptions, addenda, initial studies, Negative Declarations, Mitigated Negative Declarations, Environmental Impact Reports (EIRs), supplemental EIRs, subsequent EIRs, and program EIRs-for a variety of project types in compliance with CEQA. ESA is wellversed in both program-level and project-level environmental analyses, as well as tiering off a certified or adopted environmental document. In determining the type of environmental document that is best suited for a specific project, ESA first considers whether there is the option to streamline the CEQA analysis. Options for streamlining include a variety of exemptions. such as CEQA analysis streamlined under Senate Bill (SB) 375, or the ability to tier from an existing certified or adopted environmental document by preparing an addendum or a focused, supplemental, or subsequent environmental document.

<!-- image -->

Our work is grounded in research and review, deep knowledge of applicable laws (including relevant case law), information gathering, conducting field studies and assessments. preparing and reviewing technical reports, developing models and other decision support tools, and conducting thorough analyses of data. ESA's approach in preparing environmental documentation focuses on developing legally defensible documents that are understandable for the lay reader, while achieving efficiencies in cost and schedule to meet agency needs and preferences. Our CEQA documents are focused on presenting thorough yet comprehensible project descriptions, conducting an impact analysis relative to baseline conditions and regulatory contexts and thresholds, and developing thoughtful mitigation measures and a

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

reasonable range of alternatives to meet the needs of CEQA. The solicitation, collection, organization, and development of responses to comments is an ESA specialty. We are equipped to address projects that elicit thousands of comment letters for controversial projects such as this.

Since 2023, Bay Area cities have been processing an unprecedented number of SB 330 (Builder's Remedy) project applications that were submitted when those cities Housing Elements were out of compliance. These applications represent thousands of housing units that must be approved for housing development projects that include a minimum amount of affordable housing. Newly adopted 2024 legislation on Builder's Remedy, including Assembly Bill (AB) 1893 and AB 1886, have new implications for these types of projects. Previously, Builder's Remedy projects could take any form that the applicant chooses and could be proposed on virtually any parcel, as long as the jurisdiction lacks a substantially compliant housing element at the time of the application. AB 1893 ended this "free-for-all" approach by introducing new site restrictions, setting new density limits and allowing jurisdictions to impose certain objective local standards that would facilitate the Builder's Remedy project. ESA has been working with local jurisdictions on these types of projects to ensure that the appropriate level of environmental review is applied.

Below is a description of ESA's technical capabilities to support the CEQA documentation for this project, particularly for those topics we know to be areas of controversy for this project, including but not limited to biological resources. recreation, aesthetics, and transportation/emergency vehicle access.

## Technical Capabilities

<!-- image -->

## Air Quality, Health Risk, and Greenhouse Gas Emissions

We provide air quality, health risk, energy, and GHG emissions analyses for environmental review and compliance for a wide range of clients, including local and state agencies, utilities companies. universities and academic institutions, private developers, industrial and energy clients, and nonprofit organizations in support of CEQA documents and as stand-alone technical studies. We use best-of-class emissions models and quantification methods and incorporate robust quality assurance protocols to ensure the quality of our work products. In addition to extensive work on private development projects and plans, our AQ/GHG team has successfully analyzed a variety of natural resources, commercial, residential, and infrastructure development projects, including water recycling and desalination plants, wastewater treatment plants, river and stream flood management and restoration projects, commercial and mixed-use infill projects, small- to large-scale residential projects, and a wide range of transportation, energy, and other infrastructure projects.

Our experience also includes preparing detailed GH analysis in support of CEQA and NEPA clearance. ESA works with agencies and municipalities throughout California to assist them in complying with regulatory mandates (e.g., AB 32, SB 32. AB 1279, and SB 375), and to increase the sustainability and resilience of their communities and the infrastructure and facilities that serve them. Our project portfolio includes a wide range of planning and technical analyses related to energy and climate change. We understand that the Project will be constructed to LEED Gold standards and achieve Zero Net Energy.

Our expertise allows ESA to forecast impacts brought on by increased mobile and stationary sources, including traffic, industrial, and infrastructure emissions. We have a proven track record supporting clients in Sonoma and Marin Counties and within the jurisdiction of the BAAQMD in the completion of CEQA and NEPA documentation.

<!-- image -->

## Noise and Vibration

ESA's noise analysts have experience in acoustical analysis and modeling of project-induced sound levels. Since our founding, we have successfully prepared legally defensible noise and vibration analyses for CEQA documents, environmental noise assessments, and technical noise studies across a variety of project types, including land use and policy plans, commercial and residential development, transportation, energy, industrial, and aviation projects. Our noise and vibration team provides authoritative assessments, analyses, and design recommendations to address potential noise and vibration impacts in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations. Using sophisticated monitoring equipment, we validate noise and vibration prediction models, evaluate noise management and abatement, and model existing and future noise environments across all market sectors. Once noise levels and their sources have been determined, our experts develop defensible mitigation measures, such as sound walls and sound isolation tactics, to reduce noise impacts to the greatest extent possible.

ESA noise specialist staff is proficient with an array of acoustical modeling applications, including the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Integrated Noise Model (INM), the CadnaA three-dimensional noise propagation model, the Federal Highway Administration's (FHWA) Traffic Noise Model (TNM), and the FHWA's Roadway Construction Noise Model (RCNM). In addition to acoustical modeling, ESA has extensive experience conducting noise, vibration and hydroacoustical monitoring for short- and long-term construction projects. Our noise team is adept in the use the Larson Davis Type 1 and 2 sound level meters, spectrum analysis, Minimate IV Pro4 vibration and SpectraPlus underwater sound monitoring equipment.

<!-- image -->

## Hydrology and Water Resources

Our hydrology and water resources staff commonly perform water quality monitoring activities and studies assessing a wide array of parameters for various purposes, including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit compliance. Our respected team of geomorphologists employ project appropriate monitoring methods and techniques, including those focusing on channel morphology, inchannel habitat, and stream flow and groundwater dynamics. These staff members allow ESA to conduct peer review of hydrological studies and conduct additional research and analysis to ensure that project sites with complex hydrology are evaluated appropriately.

<!-- image -->

## Tribal Cultural and Archaeological Resources

ESA's cultural resources staff has a comprehensive knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulatory issues associated with cultural resource protection, as well as extensive experience in coordinating and negotiating with resource agencies. Our work conforms with CEQA, NEPA, and

Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. Our staff exceeds the qualifications for the Secretary of the Interior's Historic Preservation Professional Qualification Standards and the California Department of Transportation Professional Qualification Standards for each of their disciplines. Where required, our staff holds all the necessary Licenses and credentials required to conduct cultural resources analysis in California, The key cultural and tribal cultural resources staff proposed for this project work out of ESA's Petaluma office and have extensive experience working with the Sonoma County Regional Parks Department, Sonoma County Water Agency, the City of Santa Rosa, the City of Petaluma, the City of Rohnert Park, and as well as projects in Marin County (Marin Municipal Water District, North Marin Water District, County of Marin, and California State Parks Diablo District). ESA has also worked closely with Native American tribes in the area, including the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria, as well as the Mishewal-Wappo Tribe of Alexander Valley and the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation. We also bring recent and relevant experience analyzing rural agricultural properties as well as twentieth-century campus settings, including work for California Forever, Sunol Regional Wilderness, and Marin Water.

Known for our successful relationships with regulators and other project partners, ESA's cultural resources team is experienced in navigating regulatory complexities, developing appropriate mitigation, and working alongside construction teams to meet project objectives while protecting sensitive sites. From conducting complex historic architectural and archaeological resources technical studies, collaborating with institutions to preserve, curate, and manage artifact collections artifacts in curation and museum collections management and exploring submerged cultural resources, and working in collaboration with shareholders to address project effects on cultural resources, we offer a full range of experts who specialize in complex cultural resources regulatory requirements.

<!-- image -->

## Biological Resources

ESA provides expert guidance in terrestrial and aquatic wildlife biology, botany and plant ecology, habitat restoration and management, permitting, and mitigation compliance monitoring. Our biologists and ecologists integrate highly technical data into planning, regulatory, and land and resource management processes that advance sound decision-making for a variety of project types. This team functions across the entire project life cycle-from strategic planning and permitting, to study design and feld implementation, all the way through to analysis in CEQA documentation, reporting, and public outreach. We have conducted thousands of biological assessments. from due diligence/feasibility studies to comprehensive biological assessments for compliance with CEQA and various local requirements, including for numerous restoration projects in the Bay Area. With the use of advanced technologies, such as drones, stationary meters with telemetry capabilities, mobile data collection applications, statistical software, and databases, to efficiently collect, analyze, and report water quality, fisheries, wildlife, and botanical data.

<!-- image -->

## Recreation

ESA has experience working on controversial projects near sensitive recreational resources, including parkland, trails, and open space. ESA has conducted outreach to agencies that manage these recreational resources to ensure that access concerns and potential degradation effects are addressed appropriately in the environmental analysis. ESA is currently addressing these concerns through our continued work on the Donahue Highlands project, particularly with regard to a fire access road that connects to Golden Gate National Recreation Area hiking trails..

<!-- image -->

## Transportation &amp; Emergency Vehicle Access

Transportation and traffic analyses are critical to the success of development projects and longterm plans. We have teamed with our trusted subconsultant partners, Fehr &amp; Peers, to peer review applicant-prepared transportation studies, provide supplemental transportation analysis, and conduct an emergency vehicle access evaluation. The Fehr &amp; Peers team includes transportation planners and specialists, engineers, and modelers who perform traffic studies and transportation analyses for a range of projects and transportation modes. By staying on top of the latest trends in transportation analyses and modeling technology, Fehr &amp; Peers helps clients meet the challenges of planning and project development by providing specialized expertise for travel demand and behavior modeling, traffic operation forecasting, and other specialized analyses. In addition, in potentially wildfire impacted areas, Fehr &amp; Peers provide up-to-date methodology for evacuation planning in response to recent case law developments.

<!-- image -->

## Aesthetic Resources/ Visual Simulations

ESA provides analysis of aesthetic and visual resources in terms of the built environment (urban landscape), open space (including agricultural land and natural, undeveloped land), and scenic corridors (views from a recognized roadway or other linear feature having archeological, cultural, historic, natural, recreational, and/or scenic qualities). Together with our trusted subconsultant partner, PreVision Design, we will peer review the applicant's visual simulations to determine if they are sufficient to support the aesthetics analysis in the EIR. If the visual simulations are not sufficient, we will engage PreVision Design to prepare the necessary visual simulations. We have successfully partnered with PreVision Design on dozens of projects throughout the Bay Area, and their quality and attention to detail allow us to prepare robust aesthetics analyses of pre- and post-project conditions to support the analysis of visual change associated with projects.

Adam Phillips, Principal of PreVision (SBE), has 20 years of experience in architecture, 3D modeling, and environmental review studies, which has led him to become one of the established leaders in the Bay Area for aesthetic impact analysis and shadow studies. ESA has teamed with PreVision on numerous projects over the last decade in the Bay Area, including but not limited to, the 1200-1340 Bayshore Highway Project EIR, the SFO Shoreline Protection Program EIR, the California Forever Project EIR, and the Potrero Power Plant Mixed-Use Redevelopment EIR.

## About Us

ESA is a multi-disciplinary, employee-owned environmental consulting frm specializing in all aspects of project planning, environmental analysis and assessment, natural resource management, regulatory compliance, and mitigation and restoration design. ESA was founded in 1969, just outside San Francisco, at a time when the national desire for improved stewardship led to such landmark legislation as the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). ## SECTION 4 Approach

## Project Understanding

Dominican Valley LLC (applicant) proposes a residential development project on an approximately 20.79-acre site (APN: 015-163-03) located at the intersection of Magnolia Avenue and Deer Park Avenue in the City of San Rafael. The project site is designated Hillside Residential (HR) by the City of San Rafael 2040 General Plan (0.5 to 2.2 units per net acre). The project site was previously owned by Dominican University and was part of the Dominican College Campus Development Plan (ZC97-7). The project site is zoned PD (1884), containing specific development standards related to the Campus Development Plan related to agricultural research.

<!-- image -->

The proposed project involves subdividing the project site into 50 parcels and constructing 50 residential units, along with 14 Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs). The 50 residential units would include the 27 single-family homes, 17 townhomes, 14 attached JADUs, and 6 duplex units. The proposed project entitlements include a Tentative Subdivision Map and Major Environmental Design Review. The applicant submitted a SB 330 (Builder's Remedy) application for the proposed project. The proposed project does not meet the applicable maximum height and density limit set by the General Plan, nor does it meet the intended uses of the zoning designation.

## Key Issues

After reviewing the RFP and project materials, as well as researching the potential areas of controversy for the proposed project, ESA has identified the following key issues for environmental review of the proposed project:

- → Open Space, Recreation, and Public Access
- → Air Quality
- → Noise
- → Biological Resources
- &gt; Aesthetics
- → Hydrology
- Transportation and Emergency Vehicle Access
- → Utilities

Additionally, as a Builder's Remedy project, the proposed project may not be consistent with every regulation within existing City plans and policies. Therefore, special attention would be required to determine if a potential physical environmental impact could occur because of any inconsistency.

## Proposed Environmental Review Strategy

## Environmental Impact Report (proposed).

ESA anticipates a higher level of scrutiny by the City and/or the public and presents a conservative approach in the Scope of Work (see Chapter 5) to prepare a full-scope Environmental Impact Report (EIR). When there is known opposition to a project, an EIR can be prepared for greater defensibility, as courts use a more deferential standard of review when examining a lead agency's decisions in an EIR. This approach would implement the most conservative path of CEQA review, as it would present a detailed environmental analysis of the proposed project for all environmental topics. ESA understands the City staff have elected to prepare an EIR for this project in part due to the nature of the proposed project as a Builder's Remedy project and its initially identified inconsistencies with City policies. Nonetheless, the following alternatives are summarized for comparison.

## Focused EIR.

ESA also notes that CEQA review could take the form of a focused EIR that examines a handful of key environmental issues (e.g.. Aesthetics, Biological Resources, Hydrology and Water Quality, Public Services and Recreation. Transportation, etc.) that have greater potential for significant environmental impacts and/or levels of public concern. The analysis of other issues (e.g., Energy, Hazards and Hazardous Materials, Population &amp; Housing, etc.) could be presented in an attached Initial Study/CEQA Checklist and be evaluated in lesser detail. This approach could simplify preparation of the EIR by narrowing the scope of the issues to be evaluated in detail in the EIR. ESA estimates that this "focused EIR" approach could reduce EIR preparation costs by approximately 10 percent.

## Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration.

An Initial Study could be prepared first to determine the viability of using a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) for environmental review of the proposed project. An Initial Study/MND would reduce CEQA document preparation costs by approximately25 percent and result in a faster schedule compared to an EIR (estimated 10 months versus 14 months). However, as noted above, the potential for public controversy is high for the proposed project and an MND would be held to a different judicial standard of review. Therefore, ESA presents this full-scope EIR approach for City staff consideration and comment. Ultimately, City staff will select the preferred overall approach for the CEQA analysis. Should the City, as lead agency, decide an MND or a focused EIR is preferred, we welcome the opportunity to revise this proposed scope, budget, and schedule.

## Methodologies &amp; Management Philosophies

ESA employs proven project management and administrative methods to provide exceptional on-call service delivery. The following enables us to achieve project success for all our clients: :

- → Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC):
- &gt; Standards for Adequacy and Accountability;
- → Knowledge of Changes in the Law and Practice;
- Cost and Schedule Management.

## Quality Assurance/Quality Control QA/QC

ESA's commitment to quality consists of two main components: Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC). These work in tandem to produce work products for publication that are of the highest overall quality possible. Project monitoring and adherence to ESA's established QA/QC process is provided by the project manager throughout the life of the project.

The QA component applies to oversight of the preparation process for all work products and is focused on the processes by which documents are written and produced, with the goal of defect prevention. By comparison, the QC component focuses on the review process, including measures taken to ensure that deliverables satisfy the needs of the user and meet the standards of professional practice. The QA/QC program applies to all team members and work products, including those prepared by ESA subconsultants, and may consist of six major review elements of a work product

1. Self-review by contributing author/analyst,
2. Technical review by senior staff,
3. Editorial review.
4. Project manager review,
5. Project director or regional director review, and
6. Pre- and post-production review.

City of Irvine ruling, which provide critical guidance on air quality analysis and vehicle miles traveled (VMT) assessments. ## SECTION 5 Scope of Work

This detailed Scope of Work outlines ESA's proposed approach to the CEQA analysis for the proposed project and demonstrates our understanding of the core issues that will need to be addressed in the document. Note that deliverables are indicated in grey, bold body text, throughout.

## Task 1 - Project Kickoff

## Task 1.1 - Project Kickoff

ESA will work with the City and the applicant to fully understand the scope of the proposed project, this Scope of Work, and an ESA-prepared Data Request for project information that ESA will rely on to develop the environmental baseline, draft the project description, and to conduct the CEQA analysis. This task will also involve ESA's review of background studies and reports relevant to the proposed project, beyond those provided with the RFP for scoping. This task will entail one (1) kick-off meeting and site visit with the City and the applicant.

## Task 1.2: CEQA Review Strategy

ESA will prepare a draft and final CEQA review strategy memorandum for the City's consideration that outlines potential CEQA pathways for the proposed project. The memorandum will also describe if the proposed project could qualify for any CEQA streamlining provisions or exemptions, including exemptions under Public Resources Code 21083.3 (CEQA Guidelines 15183) or AB 130/SB 131. ESA assumes this would be a brief (less than 8-page) memo with one round of City review and comment. The remainder of this scope assumes that an EIR would be prepared. Should the City, as lead agency, decide an alternative form of CEQA documentation is preferred, ESA would revise this proposed scope, budget, and schedule.

## Task 2 - Notice of Preparation &amp; Scoping

ESA will prepare the baseline determination, the Notice of Preparation (NOP) of the Draft EIR (Word and PDF), and the Notice of Completion (NOC) (PDF) for the State Clearinghouse. This task also entails ESA's preparation for and participation in one (1) public scoping meeting, including preparing a presentation.

The NOP will include a project description of sufficient detail to inform the public and involved agencies and enable productive scoping of environmental issues to be addressed in the EIR. Based on information provided by the applicant. the draft project description for use in the NOP will form the basis for the more detailed Project Description chapter to be included in the EIR. It is assumed that no initial study will accompany the NOP, but rather that the NOP would list the environmental topics that would be addressed in the Draft EIR. We anticipate that we will prepare the draft NOP and NOC for up to two (2) rounds of review and comment by the City prior to finalizing each.

ESA will upload the NOP and NOC to the State Clearinghouse via CEQAsubmit. ESA will be responsible for production and mailing of the NOP to up to approximately 250 interested parties. Following the close of the 30-day public scoping period, ESA will review and catalog all scoping comments received on the NOP, provide a Scoping Comments Summary to the City, and determine with the City if any changes or refinements are required to this Scope of Work.

(Note: During this task ASC, as subconsultant to ESA, will assist with initiating the City's tribal outreach and consultation process pursuant to Assembly Bill 52 on the City's behalf.)

## Task 3 - Technical Studies

ESA will peer review all applicant-prepared technical studies and reports required to support the analysis in the EIR. This task also includes new technical studies that ESA and its subconsultants will prepare.

Based on the RFP and ESA's review of the proposed project materials, this scope assumes that ESA will receive the following technical studies to be prepared by other qualified consultants directly hired by the applicant:

- &gt; Fire Risk Assessment
- &gt; Geotechnical Report

ESA's senior technical staff will peer-review the technical studies. Fehr &amp; Peers, as a subconsultant to ESA, will lead the peer review for applicant-prepared transportation studies. The scope includes peer review of up to two (2) drafts of each technical study to confirm that the information presented is sufficient to support the CEQA analyses. ESA will highlight for discussion with City staff any peer review issues that directly compromise the integrity of the environmental analysis or clarity of the EIR or the Project Description. Draft and final peer review memoranda will be prepared.

ESA's team will prepare the following technical studies for inclusion in or appended to the EIR:

- › Biological Resources / Special Status Species Lists

## Task 4 - EIR Project Description

Concurrently with Tasks 2 and 3.1, with the primary objective of achieving a stable project description prior to commencement of the major impact analyses in Task 3.2, ESA will prepare the EIR Project Description. As mentioned in Task 2, the project description will be based largely on information provided by the applicant, including but not Limited to project objectives, site plans, elevations, construction schedules and scenarios, and operational scenarios. ESA will prepare the Draft EIR Project Description (Word and PDF) for review by the City and applicant; the revised version will be incorporated into the Administrative Draft EIR (ADEIR) (Task 5). Consistent with the RFP, the environmental analysis will not proceed until the City and the applicant have confirmed the completeness and accuracy of the Project Description.

## Task 5 - Draft EIR

## Task 5.1 - Administrative Draft EIR

ESA will prepare an Administrative Draft EIR (ADEIR) in accordance with current City and CEQA Guidelines. ESA will submit the ADEIR (Word and PDF) for up to one (1) round of review by City staff, who will provide ESA with one (1) consolidated set of non-contradictory comments. Basic sections of the ADEIR include:

## Introduction

The Introduction will briefly describe the CEQA process; the principal characteristics and objectives of the proposed project, the City's planning process, the environmental review process, and the procedural steps by which the Draft EIR will be processed.

## Executive Summary

The Summary will include a brief project description along with a brief narrative regarding alternatives, principal areas of public controversy, and unresolved issues if any. This section will include a summary table that outlines significant environmental effects, mitigation measures, and residual levels of impact significance after mitigation.

## Project Description

See Task 4 above.

## Environmental Setting, Impacts, and Mitigation Measures

This section will include an introduction that describes key environmental analysis terms used in the document and the analysis, including the impact classifications; applicability of significance criteria; the organization of each environmental topic section; the existing environmental setting (baseline) for the purpose of environmental review; and the cumulative analysis approach and setting. ESA will prepare a written recommendation to the City on an appropriate baseline for the project and related considerations.

For purposes of scoping, we have assumed that each CEQA topic will be addressed, most requiring full and detailed analysis. Some impact areas may require mitigation to reduce potential impacts. These topics will be fully analyzed in the Draft EIR and will be organized as follows:

- &gt; Aesthetics
- → Air Quality
- → Biological Resources
- &gt; Cultural Resources
- &gt; Energy
- › Geology, Soils, and Paleontological Resources
- → Greenhouse Gas Emissions
- &gt; Hazards and Hazardous Materials
- → Hydrology and Water Quality
- &gt; Land Use and Planning

Please see Technical Issues and Approaches, following Task 8, below, for discussions of the scopes of work to be conducted under each of these topics.

Within each environmental topic subsection of the Draft EIR, ESA will describe the environmental and regulatory settings. The environmental setting will describe relevant past and existing conditions in the project area and appropriate surroundings to present a comprehensive understanding of existing conditions to which the impact analysis will be measured. The regulatory settings will summarize federal, state, and local policies and regulations as they

- → Noise and Vibration
- → Population and Housing
- → Public Services and Recreation
- → Transportation
- → Tribal Cultural Resources
- → Utilities and Service Systems
- → Wildfire
- → Other topics (Agriculture and Forestry Resources, Mineral Resources)

pertain to the topics and may tier from regulatory settings in the City's General Plan EIR or other environmental plans and documents, updated as needed.

Within each environmental topic subsection of the Draft EIR, ESA will describe all applicable significance criteria, based on the CEQA Guidelines Appendix G and any thresholds established by the City or applicable regulatory agency in specific guidance documents (e.g.. Bay Area Air District ). Each section will also discuss the approach/methods. processes, and tools used to conduct the impact analysis for the topic and each criterion. ESA will confirm all proposed significance thresholds with the City prior to the initiation of substantial analysis.

For each technical topic section, the Draft EIR will assess cumulative impacts compared to baseline conditions. The cumulative analysis will determine whether there is a significant cumulative impact and if so, whether the proposed project's incremental contribution would be "cumulatively considerable." The analysis will utilize growth projections and will also consider other recent projects that are underway, or reasonably foreseeable land use development input provided by the City.

For all significant or potentially significant impacts identified in the Draft EIR, ESA will identify appropriate mitigation measures that reduce the impacts to below applicable significance thresholds, where feasible. Each mitigation measure will be specific, enforceable, not deferred to a future time, proportional to the impact they are to address; and have a clear nexus to the impact being addressed.

## Alternatives

As required by CEQA and noted in the RFP , the Draft EIR will describe a reasonable range of up to six (6) alternatives to the proposed project, including a No Project Alternative. The identification of alternatives will be based on the finding of potential impacts identified in the Draft EIR, as well as feasibility, the ability to meet at least some of the stated project objectives, and the ability to result in fewer or less severe impacts. As noted in the RFP, with the exception of two alternatives, which will be analyzed at a higher degree of specificity than normally necessary, the other four alternatives will be analyzed at a lesser level of detail than the analysis of the proposed project, but robust enough to enable decision-makers to understand the environmental differences between them.

## Statutory Sections

The Draft EIR will contain the following additional sections, as required by CEQA. ESA will prepare the discussion of each of these topics based on the analyses presented in the Draft EIR:

- → Significant Environmental Effects (including significant, unavoidable effects)
- → Growth-Inducing Impacts
- → Significant Irreversible Environmental Changes
- → Effects Found Not to be Significant

ESA will also include sections in the Draft EIR listing Preparers of the EIR. Persons and Agencies/Organizations Consulted, and References.

## Appendices

Supporting technical studies identified in Task 3 may be included as appendices to the Draft EIR, as appropriate. Other appendices will include the NOP and scoping comments addressed in Task 2. A Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plan (MMRP) will be included as an appendix to the Draft EIR and refined in the Final EIR.

This proposal assumes the City will provide one (1) set of consolidated non-contradictory comments on the ADEIR. substantive changes. A draft MMRP will be submitted with the Screencheck Draft EIR, which will be included as a Draft EIR appendix.

ESA assumes that the City will be responsible for posting at the site and publishing notices in the newspaper.

ESA will submit an Administrative Record (consisting of sources referenced in the Draft EIR) to the City in electronic (PDF) format prior to publication of the Draft EIR.

ESA assumes that up to one (1) public hearing to receive oral testimony on the Draft EIR would be conducted during the 45-day Draft EIR public review period by the Planning Commission. ## Task 7 - Public Hearings &amp; EIR Certification

## Task 7.1 - EIR Hearings

ESA will participate in up to two (2) public hearings before the City Planning Commission and up to two (2) public hearings before the City Council related to consideration of certification of the EIR and approval of the proposed project. However, ESA is sensitive to the public hearing limitation for SB 330 projects (5 total) and assumes that no more than three (3) public hearings would occur, considering the NOP scoping meeting and Draft EIR hearing. We assume that the ESA team will support City staff by assisting with preparation of a PowerPoint presentation and answering questions during the hearing(s) on the EIR certification. ESA will be responsible for the production and mailing of a NOA of the Final EIR and public hearing notice to up to approximately 250 interested parties and commenters for the first certification hearing on the Final EIR. Production and mailing of public hearing notices for up to two (2) additional public hearings will also be prepared.

## Task 7.2 - CEQA Findings &amp; Resolution

ESA will prepare a draft findings resolution, including overriding considerations, if necessary, and convert EIR mitigation measures to a list of conditions for project approval for one (1) round of City Attorney review (Word and PDF).

## Task 7.3 - Notice of Determination

ESA will coordinate with City staff to prepare a Notice of Determination (NOD) for City staff or applicant to file with the County Clerk within five (5) days following the first approval related to the proposed project. This scope assumes that the state and County fees will be paid directly to the County Clerk by the applicant.

## Task 8 - Project Management &amp; Meetings

This task covers project management activities as follows and assumes a 14-month schedule:

## Task 8.1 - Meetings (14-months)

- &gt; Attendance at up to one virtual team meetings per month, in addition to informal meetings (up to two per month). for an approximately 14-month period (separate from Project kick-off meeting (Task 1.11 and ADEIR workshops (Tasks 5.21).

## Task 8.2 - Project Management

- → Day-to-day coordination and consultation with the City and other staff as needed.
- › Monitoring project status in terms of staffing, budget, and schedule.
- &gt; Monthly invoices and status reports.
- › Management of all work efforts, maintain consistency in project understanding and approach, maintain action item lists and information requests, address and respond to issues as they arise, and distribute the project information needed for preparation of the CEQA documentation.
